## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A two-fascicle Eastern-Hàn Buddha-biography sūtra continuing the narrative from the Bodhi-tree onward — the *Zhōng* ("middle") of the title indicates the middle phase of the Buddha-biography after the awakening, complementing *[Xiūxíng běnqǐ jīng 修行本起經 (T184)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0040)* which covers the prior phases (the *běn* / "origin"). The Taishō head-note identifies the sūtra as 「次名四部僧」 ("next to be called the *Sūtra of the Four-fold Saṃgha*") and notes that it draws material from the *Dīrghāgama* (出長阿含). Translated by [曇果](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E6%9E%9C) Tánguǒ and [康孟詳](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BA%B7%E5%AD%9F%E8%A9%B3) Kāng Mèngxiáng. Signature: 「後漢西域沙門曇果共康孟詳譯」.

**Abstract**

T196's translation can be dated to Jiàn'ān 建安 12 = 207 CE based on the *Chū sānzàng jì jí* records. It is the post-awakening Buddha-biography continuing T184; the two together constitute the canonical Eastern-Hàn Chinese Buddha-biography cycle. The Indic source is conventionally identified with a now-lost *Madhyamāgama* / *Dīrghāgama*-class Buddha-biography of the Mahāsāṃghika or Sarvāstivāda tradition, with internal evidence (the head-note's reference to 出長阿含) suggesting a *Dīrghāgama*-related Indic exemplar.
